_: Scenes for word cards — Session 18. EN vignette + one JP line. src 'grammar:<point>' means the line is reused from that grammar point's examples and is already in the reviewer queue; src 'new' means the Japanese is new and NEEDS REVIEW. Vignettes are fiction and carry no factual claims.

医者.scene: Lunch with a coworker drifts into family. You get through your brother's job in one sentence, and it lands — she nods and asks which hospital.
医者.jp: 兄は医者になりました。
医者.en: My older brother became a doctor.

風邪.scene: The morning greeting comes back sounding blocked. Your coworker waves it off before you can ask.
風邪.jp: ちょっと風邪気味です。
風邪.en: I'm coming down with a bit of a cold.

駅.scene: The apartment agent asks how you'll commute. It is the first question everyone asks about a new place, and this is the stock answer shape.
駅.jp: 家から駅まで歩きます。
駅.en: I walk from home to the station.

遅れる.scene: Six of you at the restaurant, one chair empty. Someone checks the group chat and relays the news.
遅れる.jp: クリスさんは少し遅れるということです。
遅れる.en: Word is Chris will be a little late.

予約.scene: You're still comparing hostels for the Kyoto weekend when your friend looks up from her phone, already finished.
予約.jp: ホテルを予約しておきました。

東京.scene: First round of introductions at the community class. Where you live comes before what you do.

会議.scene: Monday morning. The whiteboard by the office door has one line on it and everyone has already read it.
会議.jp: 会議は三時に始まります。

仕事.scene: The izakaya at nine on a weeknight — half the tables are groups still in office clothes. Your coworker explains yesterday evening in one line.
仕事.jp: 仕事が終わってから飲みに行きました。
仕事.en: After work ended, we went drinking.

予定.scene: The hostel common room, maps open. The traveller across the table has tomorrow settled.
予定.jp: 明日、京都へ行く予定です。
予定.en: The plan is to go to Kyoto tomorrow.

説明.scene: The ward office clerk has said something important, fast, twice. This sentence is the polite way to stop the conveyor belt.
説明.jp: もう一度説明していただけますか。
説明.en: Could I ask you to explain that once more?

晩ご飯.scene: Your phone buzzes on the walk home from the station — a message from your host mother that settles the evening.
晩ご飯.jp: 晩ご飯はもう作ってあります。

お茶.scene: End of the meal, the server hovers. The question is always the same pair of options.
お茶.jp: コーヒーかお茶を飲みます。

店.scene: You mention needing a rice cooker and your neighbour points down the shopping street without breaking stride.
店.en: That shop is cheap, you know.

連絡.scene: The train has been stopped between stations for ten minutes. All down the carriage, phones come out for the same purpose.
連絡.jp: 遅れている間に、会社に連絡しました。
連絡.en: While it was delayed, I contacted the office.

約束.scene: Your friend is visibly exhausted and coming to the party anyway. You ask why; the answer is the whole of Japanese social logic in one sentence.
約束.jp: 約束したので、行かないわけにはいかない。
約束.en: I promised, so I can't very well not go.

準備.scene: Post-mortem over coffee after the presentation went sideways. Your coworker is honest about the cause.
準備.jp: 準備しなかったばかりに、失敗しました。
準備.en: Precisely because I didn't prepare, it failed.

最近.scene: Two women behind you on the bus, laughing at themselves. You catch the whole exchange and understand it.

荷物.scene: Stairs at the small station, no elevator, an older man eyeing a suitcase. This is the sentence that offers.
荷物.jp: 荷物を持ちましょうか。

電車.scene: You name your destination and the hostel owner pulls a face at your route, then offers the local knowledge.
電車.jp: 電車よりバスのほうが安いです。
電車.en: The bus is cheaper than the train.

結果.scene: The share-house meeting about the noise finally ends. The notice on the fridge the next morning starts with this.
結果.jp: よく話し合った結果、こうなりました。
結果.en: As a result of talking it through properly, this is what we decided.

場合.scene: The neighbourhood festival flyer on the notice board, one line of small print at the bottom that everyone checks the sky against.
場合.jp: 雨の場合は中止になります。
場合.en: In case of rain, it will be cancelled.

受付.scene: The clinic door slides open onto a counter, a clipboard, and a pen on a string. The receptionist says it before you reach the desk.
受付.jp: 受付で名前を書いてください。
受付.en: Please write your name at reception.

保険証.scene: First visit to any clinic in Japan opens with the same three words at the counter, palm out, before a single symptom is discussed.
保険証.jp: 保険証をお願いします。

会計.scene: Dinner for four winds down and the server appears with one question that decides who owes what.
会計.jp: お会計はご一緒ですか。

番号.scene: The pharmacy hands you a small paper ticket instead of your name. The wall screen explains the system.

窓口.scene: The bank machine prints a slip, and the guard reads it and points across the lobby.

忘れる.scene: Rainy evening train. As the doors open, the announcement makes the same plea it makes at every stop, and tonight the umbrella racks prove why.
忘れる.jp: 傘を忘れないでください。

写真を撮る.scene: The temple gate is magnificent and there is a small sign beside it. This is the question to ask before raising the phone.
写真を撮る.jp: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか。
写真を撮る.en: Is it all right to take photos here?

雨が降る.scene: The konbini clerk glances past you at the grey sky while bagging your onigiri, and offers the evening forecast unprompted.
雨が降る.jp: 午後から雨が降るそうです。
雨が降る.en: I hear it's going to rain from the afternoon.

薬を飲む.scene: The pharmacist circles two spots on the medicine envelope with a red pen and says it slowly, because it matters.
薬を飲む.jp: 一日三回、薬を飲んでください。
薬を飲む.en: Please take the medicine three times a day.
